mn127:2.9: “Sir, the chamberlain Pañcakaṅga bows with his head to your feet, and he says:
mn127:2.10: ‘Sir, would Venerable Anuruddha please accept tomorrow’s meal from Pañcakaṅga together with three other mendicants?
mn127:2.11: And might Venerable Anuruddha please come earlier than usual,
mn127:2.12: for Pañcakaṅga has many duties, and much work to do for the king.’”
